title: Electrical Systems: Circuits and Components
summary: Circuit components and symbols, series and parallel circuits, conductors and insulators, Ohm's law, and the systems approach of input, process and output.

notes.text: Technological systems can be described as **input → process → output**. In an electrical circuit:

rows: Wires, resistors, switches controlling the current
Bulb, LED, buzzer, motor, heating element

notes.text: An **LED** must always be connected the right way round and usually needs a **resistor** in series to stop too much current from damaging it.

notes.title: Cells in series and parallel
notes.problem: You have two 1,5 V cells. What voltage do you get with them in series? In parallel?
steps: In series the voltages add: 1,5 + 1,5 = 3 V.
In parallel the voltage stays the same, at 1,5 V, but the cells last longer.
notes.answer: 3 V in series; 1,5 V in parallel.

notes.title: Using Ohm's law
notes.problem: A 9 V battery is connected to a 450 Ω resistor. Calculate the current.

items: **Conductors**: copper, aluminium, graphite; used for wires and connections.
**Insulators**: plastic, rubber, glass, dry wood; used to cover wires and make handles.
Never touch mains electricity (230 V). Keep water away from electrical appliances. Do not overload plugs.
A **short circuit** (current bypassing the components) causes wires to overheat and can start a fire.

questions.prompt: A 12 V supply is connected to a 6 Ω resistor. Calculate the current.
A current of 0,5 A flows through a 20 Ω resistor. Calculate the voltage across it.
In a parallel circuit, if one bulb blows the others go out.
Classify each component in a torch.
Why is a resistor usually connected in series with an LED?
questions.memo:
✓ It limits the current (1)
✓ so that too much current does not damage/burn out the LED (1)

questions.prompt: Give ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of a series circuit.
questions.memo:
✓ Advantage: simple / uses less current, so the battery lasts longer (1)
✓ Disadvantage: if one component fails all stop / bulbs dimmer (1)

questions.prompt: What is a short circuit and why is it dangerous?
questions.memo:
✓ Current takes a path of very low resistance, bypassing the components (1)
✓ A very large current flows and overheats the wires, which can cause a fire (1)
